name: Hans Trapp
description: The Alsatian bogeyman who comes with the Christkindel to frighten the naughty

debut.title: Alsatian Christmas tradition
debut.era: legend built on a real knight of the late 1400s

legend: In Alsace the Christkindel, a figure in white bearing gifts, doesn't visit alone. Behind it comes Hans Trapp, a dark, frightening figure who growls at the children and threatens the naughty. His legend borrows the name of a real man, Hans von Trotha, a knight of the late 1400s who fought a bitter feud with the abbey of Wissembourg and was excommunicated for it. In the folk telling he became a greedy, godless brute who was finally struck down by heaven and now comes back each Christmas to scare children into being good.

myths.claim: Hans Trapp is based on a real person.
myths.explanation: His name comes from Hans von Trotha, a knight who feuded with the abbey of Wissembourg in the late 1400s.

myths.claim: Hans Trapp brings the presents in Alsace.
myths.explanation: The Christkindel brings the gifts. Hans Trapp is the threat that comes with them.

myths.claim: Hans Trapp is mostly a figure of Alsace and Lorraine.
myths.explanation: He belongs to the Christmas traditions of north-east France, close to the German border.

powers: The shadow of a real knight's bad name
weaknesses: A legend that already ended badly for him
legacy: Christmas markets in Alsace, where Hans Trapp still makes appearances
The castle of Berwartstein in the Palatinate, Hans von Trotha's real home
